claims.text: Applying a conformal 20–50 nm Cu coating to W particles by ALD before spark-plasma sintering will produce a near-perfect, continuous W/Cu interphase.
The ALD-coated composite will have higher thermal conductivity than vapor-coated W powders processed by conventional SPS.
The ALD-coated composite will have greater mechanical durability under irradiation than vapor-coated W powders processed by conventional SPS.
The starting W particles or preformed W regions may carry native or passivating surface layers.
ALD can deposit a conformal Cu layer on W particles at 200–300 °C under inert conditions.
SPS below 900 °C preserves the integrity of the ALD Cu coating.
Inert or vacuum processing prevents oxidation during fabrication.
A nanoscale Cu interlayer will create uniform, intimate contact at W/Cu interfaces.
A nanoscale Cu interlayer will suppress interfacial voids and gaps.
A conformal ALD Cu coating enhances wettability between W and Cu during sintering.
Enhanced W/Cu wettability leads to improved interfacial bonding.
The continuous Cu interphase minimizes void formation.
The continuous Cu interphase minimizes W/Cu phase separation.
Reduced interfacial defects and a continuous interphase improve thermal transport.
Reduced interfacial defects and a continuous interphase improve mechanical resilience under fusion-relevant irradiation.
Vapor-coated W powders processed by conventional SPS exhibit occasional interfacial voids and phase separation.
The ALD coating remains stable during SPS conducted below 900 °C.
Exceeding an unspecified thermal threshold causes the ALD Cu layer to degrade or agglomerate.
